LESSON: FICTION AND NON - FICTION 9.3.1 FICTION: ANTHOLOGY OF SHORT STORIES FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we study short stories in literature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. discuss the themes in short stories for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse language and style in short stories for critical analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate thematic concerns in short stories to values

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. discuss the themes in short stories for literary appreciation,

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. analyse language and style in short stories for critical analysis,

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. relate thematic concerns in short stories to values

   Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or offline for thematic concerns in short stories and share in class. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or offline for thematic concerns in short stories and share in class. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non - Fiction 9.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
